devices.native: Native layout: a device built for the code, IBM's planned layout for bivariate bicycle codes
devices.native_lr: Native layout with long-range couplers as noisy as IBM's remote couplers
devices.real_bicycle: IBM bicycle module: gross-code toric layout with long-range c-couplers (288 qubits)
devices.real_bicycle_lr: IBM bicycle module with c-couplers as noisy as remote couplers (288 qubits)
devices.real_bicycle_lr_2_qpus: IBM bicycle modules, 2 chained, noisy c-couplers (576 qubits)

slices.qldpc_ibm_projected: qLDPC codes on larger IBM devices (projected)
slices.bb_native: Bivariate bicycle codes in IBM's native layout
slices.qldpc_atoms: qLDPC codes on neutral atoms and trapped ions
slices.reference: Reference: all codes on an all-to-all device
slices.paper_dqc: Paper experiment: one QPU vs distributed QPUs
slices.paper_topology: Paper experiment: codes on sparse devices

slice_descriptions.qldpc_ibm: qLDPC codes compiled onto IBM Heron, Loon/Nighthawk (one or two QPUs) and Flamingo (one or three QPUs), at the devices' noise and, for Loon and Flamingo, at ten times lower noise.
slice_descriptions.qldpc_ibm_projected: qLDPC codes too large for any IBM device, on projected chains of as many Loon or Flamingo QPUs as they need, at ten times lower noise.
slice_descriptions.qldpc_bicycle: qLDPC codes and the paper's codes on the 288-qubit module of IBM's bicycle architecture, with its long-range couplers as good as local ones or as noisy as remote ones, at IBM noise and ten times lower.
slice_descriptions.qldpc_bicycle_chain: qLDPC codes too large for one bicycle module, on as many modules as they need, linked by remote couplers, at ten times lower noise.
slice_descriptions.bb_native: Bivariate bicycle codes placed one to one on IBM's planned layout for them, with long-range couplers as good as local ones or as noisy as remote ones, to compare with the same codes compiled onto Loon and Flamingo.
slice_descriptions.qldpc_atoms: qLDPC codes on neutral atoms (the Harvard/MIT array, Infleqtion) and Quantinuum's trapped ions, at the devices' own noise. Any two qubits can interact after a move, so no SWAPs are needed.
slice_descriptions.readout_700: The codes of the IBM datasets again, with 700 ns readout instead of the 1.56 us of IBM's calibration data, to see how much faster readout would help.
slice_descriptions.willow_surface: The surface code memory on Google Willow at distances 3 to 7, compiled by Qiskit and placed on the grid as in Google's below-threshold experiment (Nature 638, 920, 2025), to compare with its measurements.
slice_descriptions.floquet_devices: Floquet codes (honeycomb, planar honeycomb, hyperbolic and semi-hyperbolic) on IBM, Google, trapped-ion and neutral-atom devices.
slice_descriptions.noise_scaling: Codes at several distances on IBM, Google and neutral-atom devices, with every error probability of the device's noise multiplied by 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 or 1: where each device crosses threshold, and how much better it must get.
slice_descriptions.basis_x: The same memory experiments with the logical |+> state prepared and measured in the X basis, paired with their Z-basis results: the Willow surface code, codes on IBM, Google and neutral-atom devices at their own noise, Bacon-Shor and XZZX in both bases, and asymmetric codes under uniform SD6 noise.
slice_descriptions.reference: Every code at its default schedule on an all-to-all device with uniform SD6 circuit noise: the common baseline that makes the device datasets comparable.
slice_descriptions.paper_dqc: The configurations of the ECCentric paper's (SIGMETRICS 2026) comparison of one QPU with distributed QPUs, rerun with the current, corrected simulator (noise model, Steane readout, single-QPU devices) and decoded with BP-OSD as in the paper.
slice_descriptions.paper_topology: The configurations of the ECCentric paper's (SIGMETRICS 2026) experiments on device topologies (grid, cube and all-to-all connectivity; Willow, Apollo and Infleqtion), rerun with the current simulator, which places codes on a device instead of qubit by qubit and so avoids needless SWAPs; decoded with BP-OSD as in the paper.
